# Fitness status — 2026-09-14

Window: 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-14 (14 days)

## Summary

**Training load & consistency.** Nine activities across the 14-day window, spread over 8 active days (Sep 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 11, 12, 13) with a 3-day rest block Sep 8–10: six runs (Sep 1: 6.0 km, Sep 2: 7.3 km, Sep 4: 10.0 km, Sep 6: 5.0 km, Sep 11: 9.2 km, Sep 13: 5.5 km), two rides (Sep 7: 44.2 km, Sep 12: 29.9 km), and one short walk (Sep 13: 2.0 km). Total distance ~119 km, total moving time ~10.7 hours. The first week (Sep 1–7) was the busiest stretch (5 sessions in 7 days, including the longest run and the longest ride), followed by a clear 3-day taper/rest, then a second, lighter cluster (Sep 11–13, bike + run + walk) and no activity yet today (Sep 14). Overall pattern: solid consistency with a deliberate rest block mid-window rather than a decline.

**Recovery signals.** Training readiness climbed steadily from a LOW 47 on Sep 1 to a PRIME 100 on Sep 10 (the rest day), then eased back down through the second activity cluster to 76 (Sep 12), 75 (Sep 13) and 66/MODERATE on Sep 14 — a normal post-training dip, not a worrying trend. HRV status was UNBALANCED/BALANCED-mixed in the first week (weekly average ~44–45) and has been consistently BALANCED since Sep 12, with weekly average up to 52–53 — an improving signal. Resting heart rate has no data for Sep 1–7 (not reported by Garmin for those days), then sat in a healthy 45–54 bpm band from Sep 8 onward, dipping to a low of 45 on the Sep 10 rest day and settling around 48–51 since — stable, no elevation. Sleep data is likewise only available from Sep 9 onward: scores of 85, 95, 74, 85, 80, 70, with one short night (5.8 h, score 74) on Sep 11 right before the second training cluster, and a milder dip (score 70, ~8 h) on the most recent night (Sep 13→14) coinciding with the lower readiness score today. Stress readings (available from Sep 8) stayed in a moderate-to-low range (16–41 average), nothing notable.

**VO2max trend.** Per-activity VO2max values from running activities, in chronological order: Sep 1 → 40, Sep 2 → 40, Sep 4 → 39, Sep 6 → 39, Sep 11 → 39, Sep 13 → 40. This is flat within normal noise (a single point of jitter, no real change). The account-level trend in `training_status` (`mostRecentVO2Max.generic`) was null through Sep 10, then populated from Sep 11 onward at 40 (precise 39.6), rising marginally to 40.3 by Sep 13 — consistent with the per-activity readings and confirming a stable, not declining or improving, aerobic fitness level. The cycling account-level trend remains null for the whole window (not enough qualifying rides), so cycling VO2max can't be assessed from `training_status`, and the ride activities don't carry `vO2MaxValue`.

**Observations / suggestions.** (1) The Sep 8–10 rest block clearly paid off — readiness peaked at 100 and resting HR hit its lowest (45) right after it — so this kind of periodic 2–3 day break looks effective and worth repeating. (2) The short night before Sep 11's session (5.8 h) didn't visibly hurt that day's run (still 9.2 km, VO2 39), but readiness dropped from 94 to 76 by the next day, suggesting sleep debt catches up within a day or two — worth prioritizing sleep the night before harder sessions. (3) VO2max has been flat at 39–40 for two weeks across six runs; if the goal is to raise it, the current mix of steady 5–10 km runs may need a structured intensity stimulus (intervals or tempo work) rather than more of the same volume.
